title: kv-cache: defragmentation + paging + spillover eviction improvements
author: Marina Karpov
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and spillover have been a recurring source of increased memory pressure and unpredictable tail latency in multi-tenant workloads. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements: adaptive defragmentation heuristic, smarter paging thresholds, and prioritized spillover eviction to reduce end-to-end memory usage and improve latency stability. Summary of changes: 1) Defragmentation work queue: background defrag task that compacts fragmented KV entries with low CPU impact, triggered adaptively when fragmentation ratio > 0.35 or after extended high-allocation periods. 2) Paging tuning: introduce a multi-tier paging threshold (soft/target/hard) so that paging to host memory only happens when soft->target margins are exceeded and only moves cold prefixes first. 3) Spillover eviction priority: prefer evicting large, low-reuse segments (long tail keys) and avoid evicting session-active prefixes; this is implemented by tracking recent-access heat (LRU window) and size-weighted scoring. 4) Metrics+tracing: added fragmentation_ratio, defrag_runs_total, paging_moved_bytes, spillover_evictions_{count,bytes}, and per-tenant eviction_reasons metric with tags. 5) Rollout/fallback: feature flag redwood.kv.defrag_v2 with dynamic thresholds and graceful fallback to previous policy on error. Microbenchmarks: - End-to-end throughput on perf-canary (gpt-medium-like workload) shows 5-8% p99 latency reduction under heavy concurrency and 12-18% reduction in average host paging bytes. - Memory footprint: mean GPU-resident KV bytes reduced by ~9% in tests with long-context sessions due to compaction. Testing: unit tests for defrag correctness, integration tests with perf-canary cluster, and a new chaos test that simulates noisy tenants and forced OOM conditions. Backwards compat: on-by-default for new clusters; feature-flag gated for rolling upgrades. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global with monitoring playbook. See linked Linear tickets for background.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive background defragmentation, soft/target/hard paging thresholds, and prioritized spillover eviction. Expected benefits: reduced GPU-resident KV memory, reduced host paging, and improved p99 latency under heavy concurrency. Feature is behind a runtime feature flag for staged rollout.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover defrag correctness and eviction scoring. Integration tests run against perf-canary and include chaos scenarios to simulate noisy tenants. Added microbench harness for eviction CPU/latency overhead. Observability dashboards updated to surface fragmentation_ratio and paging metrics.
rollback_plan: Toggle redwood.kv.defrag_v2 feature flag to false to revert to legacy eviction/paging behavior. Monitor paging_moved_bytes and p99 latency for 10 minutes after toggling. If issues persist, rollback to previous runtime image and open incident ticket.
